headline: I turn messy operational work into tools a small team can run.
intro: I build internal tools, dashboards and AI-assisted workflows for the parts of a business that usually live in spreadsheets and inboxes: sales prep, site screening, client operations and finance.
body:
Most of my projects start the same way: a small team doing important work by hand, with the knowledge spread across documents, websites and people's heads. I like finding the structure in that work and building something that makes it faster without hiding how it works.

When I use language models, I put them last in the pipeline. Rules, scoring and data checks run in plain code first, and the model writes from a fact sheet it can't wander away from. Every claim needs a source, outputs are checked against a schema, and there's always a fallback, so a team can trust what's in front of them.

I care about the last mile too: interfaces that are quick to read, printable one-page outputs, guided tours for new users, and demos anyone can open in a browser.

focus.title: Operations tools
focus.body: CRMs, dashboards and workflow apps that replace spreadsheets and manual prep for small teams.

focus.title: Grounded AI
focus.body: LLM features with citations, schema checks and rule-based fallbacks, so the output is something you can act on.

focus.title: Data and maps
focus.body: Geospatial pipelines, scoring models and visualisations that turn public data into shortlists and decisions.
